title: AI and bots have officially taken over the internet, report finds
summary: AI and bots have officially taken over the internet, report finds    CNBC
editorial_override: AI and bots officially taken over the internet — core narrative for data infrastructure
post_en:
Bots now generate more internet traffic than humans. It's official.

The latest global traffic analysis confirms what many suspected: automated systems — scrapers, AI agents, crawlers, and botnets — now account for the majority of all web requests.

What this means in practice:
→ More than half the "visitors" hitting your website aren't people
→ Analytics dashboards are lying to you about real engagement
→ Ad impressions are increasingly served to machines
→ Every dataset scraped from the web is contaminated with bot-generated content

For data infrastructure teams, this isn't just a headline — it's a fundamental shift in how web data must be collected and validated.

When bots talk to bots, the signal-to-noise ratio collapses. Raw scraping without filtering is now actively dangerous for AI training, market research, and competitive intelligence.

The companies that win are building three capabilities:
1. Bot-vs-human traffic classification at the infrastructure level
2. Data provenance tracking from collection through delivery
3. Quality scoring that separates genuine content from synthetic noise

The internet we built for humans is now primarily used by machines. Your data pipeline should reflect that reality.

#BotTraffic #DataInfrastructure #WebData

Что это значит на практике:
→ Больше половины «посетителей» вашего сайта — не люди
→ Аналитика врёт о реальном вовлечении
→ Рекламные показы всё чаще обслуживают машины
→ Каждый датасет из веба загрязнён бот-контентом

Когда боты разговаривают с ботами, соотношение сигнал/шум рушится. Сырой скрейпинг без фильтрации теперь опасен для AI-обучения и конкурентной разведки.

Побеждают те, кто строит:
1. Классификацию бот/человек на уровне инфраструктуры
2. Отслеживание провенанса данных
3. Скоринг качества, отделяющий настоящий контент от синтетического шума

Интернет, построенный для людей, теперь в основном используется машинами.

title: Poison AI Training Data Scrapers
summary: Article URL: https://github.com/austin-weeks/miasma Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47552115 Points: 4 # Comments: 1
editorial_override: Poison AI Training Data Scrapers — anti-scraping defense, directly relevant
post_en:
A new open-source tool lets website owners poison the data that AI scrapers collect.

It works by detecting automated crawlers and serving them subtly corrupted content — wrong facts, garbled text, misleading statistics — while showing humans the real page.

This is the next escalation in the web scraping arms race.

Why it matters:
→ Passive defenses (robots.txt, rate limits) are easily bypassed
→ Active poisoning makes scraped data unreliable without the scraper knowing
→ AI models trained on poisoned data produce worse outputs
→ This shifts the economic calculus: scraping without permission now carries quality risk, not just legal risk

For legitimate data collection companies, this is actually good news.

When unauthorized scraping becomes unreliable, the value of trusted, permission-based data access increases dramatically.

The data infrastructure market is splitting in two:
• Providers who can guarantee data quality through legitimate access partnerships
• Everyone else, who can't tell if their data was poisoned before collection

If your business depends on web data, ask: can your provider prove the data wasn't corrupted at source?

#WebScraping #DataQuality #AITraining

title: ‘Manners for machines’: how new rules could stop AI scrapers destroying the internet
summary: ‘Manners for machines’: how new rules could stop AI scrapers destroying the internet    Digital Information World
editorial_override: Manners for machines: new rules could stop AI scrapers — scraping regulation
post_en:
"Manners for machines" — that's how regulators are framing the next wave of AI scraping rules.

New proposals across the EU, UK, and California would require AI systems to:
→ Identify themselves when accessing websites (no more hiding behind residential IPs)
→ Respect machine-readable opt-out signals
→ Maintain audit logs of what data was collected and from where
→ Provide compensation mechanisms for content creators

This isn't hypothetical anymore. Draft legislation is moving through committees.

The implications for data infrastructure are massive:

Every proxy request, every crawl job, every data pipeline will need to answer: "Did you have permission to collect this?"

Companies still operating on the "scrape first, ask questions never" model have maybe 12-18 months before this becomes legally enforceable.

The smart players are already building:
• Transparent crawler identification
• Consent verification at the request level
• Automated compliance documentation
• Legitimate data access partnerships

The wild west of web scraping isn't ending because of technology. It's ending because of law.

Prepare now, or prepare to explain later.

#WebScraping #DataRegulation #AICompliance

→ Вести аудит-логи собранных данных
→ Обеспечивать компенсации создателям контента

title: Proxy IP is clean but sessions still get flagged – it's probably DNS
summary: Article URL: https://voidmob.com/blog/dns-leak-proxy-killer-carrier-native-dns Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47533811 Points: 1 # Comments: 0
editorial_override: Proxy IP clean but sessions flagged by DNS — deep technical proxy insight
post_en:
Your proxy IP is clean. Your headers are perfect. Your fingerprint passes every check.

But your sessions keep getting flagged. Why?

It's probably your DNS.

A deep technical analysis reveals one of the most overlooked vectors in proxy detection: DNS leakage.

Here's what happens:
→ You route HTTP traffic through a proxy in Germany
→ But your DNS queries still resolve through Google's 8.8.8.8 in the US
→ The target site sees a German IP making requests that resolve DNS from Virginia
→ Instant flag. Session killed.

This affects every proxy user, from enterprise data teams to individual researchers.

The fix isn't complicated, but most proxy setups completely ignore it:
1. Route DNS through the same exit node as your traffic
2. Use DNS-over-HTTPS through the proxy tunnel
3. Verify with a DNS leak test BEFORE running production jobs
4. Monitor for DNS leaks continuously, not just during setup

I've seen teams spend months debugging "bad IPs" when the real problem was a 2-minute DNS configuration.

The most expensive proxy pool in the world is worthless if your DNS gives you away.

#ProxyInfrastructure #WebScraping #DataCollection
post_ru:

Но сессии продолжают блокироваться. Почему?

Скорее всего, DNS.

Глубокий технический анализ раскрывает один из самых недооценённых векторов детекции прокси: утечку DNS.

Что происходит:
→ HTTP-трафик идёт через прокси в Германии
→ Но DNS-запросы резолвятся через Google 8.8.8.8 в США
→ Целевой сайт видит немецкий IP с DNS из Вирджинии
→ Мгновенный флаг. Сессия убита.

Исправление несложное, но большинство его игнорируют:
1. Маршрутизируйте DNS через тот же выходной узел
2. Используйте DNS-over-HTTPS через прокси-туннель
3. Проверяйте DNS leak test ДО продакшн-задач
4. Мониторьте утечки DNS постоянно

Самый дорогой прокси-пул бесполезен, если DNS вас выдаёт.

#ProxyInfrastructure #WebScraping #DataCollection

title: The Bot Flood Is Here. News Orgs Need to Stop Feeding It For Free
summary: The Bot Flood Is Here. News Orgs Need to Stop Feeding It For Free    tvnewscheck.com
editorial_override: Bot Flood Is Here, news orgs must stop feeding it — bot traffic + content access
post_en:
News organizations are feeding the bot flood for free. And they're finally waking up to the cost.

A new analysis shows that major publishers are serving 60-70% of their page views to automated systems — AI crawlers, content aggregators, and scraping bots.

The math is brutal:
→ Each bot page view costs bandwidth, CDN fees, and server resources
→ Bots don't click ads, don't subscribe, don't share on social media
→ AI companies train on the content and compete with the publishers who created it
→ The more a publisher invests in quality content, the more valuable they become as a scraping target

This is the content industry's tragedy of the commons.

Publishers are now responding with:
• Aggressive bot detection and blocking
• Paywalled content that requires authentication
• Legal action against AI companies using their content
• Licensing deals that monetize data access

For data infrastructure companies, this signals a permanent shift.

Free, open access to publisher content is ending. The future is authenticated, licensed, metered data access.

Build your data pipeline around that reality — or watch it break.

#ContentIndustry #BotTraffic #DataAccess

title: Show HN: Imrobot – Reverse CAPTCHA that verifies AI agents, not humans
summary: Article URL: https://github.com/leopechnicki/im_robot Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47528383 Points: 1 # Comments: 0
editorial_override: Reverse CAPTCHA verifies AI agents not humans — bot detection innovation
post_en:
What if CAPTCHAs verified AI agents instead of blocking them?

Imrobot flips the entire bot detection model on its head. Instead of proving you're human, it proves you're a legitimate AI agent — with verified identity, declared purpose, and auditable behavior.

Why this matters more than another CAPTCHA alternative:

The web is entering an age where most traffic is automated. Blocking ALL bots is no longer viable — you'd block AI shopping agents, search indexers, accessibility tools, and legitimate data collection.

The new question isn't "are you human?" It's "are you authorized?"

Imrobot's approach:
→ AI agents register and receive cryptographic credentials
→ Each request carries proof of identity and declared intent
→ Website owners set granular policies: allow research bots, block scrapers, rate-limit indexers
→ Every interaction is logged and auditable

This is where bot detection is heading. Not walls that block everything, but gates that verify and authorize.

For proxy and data infrastructure providers: this model means your clients will need verifiable agent identities, not just clean IPs.

The era of anonymous automated access is ending. The era of authenticated machine-to-machine trust is beginning.

#BotDetection #AIAgents #WebInfrastructure

→ Каждый запрос несёт proof of identity и объявленный intent
→ Владельцы сайтов задают гранулярные политики
→ Каждое взаимодействие логируется и аудируется

Для прокси-провайдеров: клиентам нужны верифицируемые идентичности агентов, а не только чистые IP.

Эра анонимного автоматического доступа заканчивается. Начинается эра аутентифицированного доверия машина-к-машине.

title: Wikipedia Bans AI-Generated Content
summary: “In recent months, more and more administrative reports centered on LLM-related issues, and editors were being overwhelmed.”
editorial_override: Wikipedia bans AI-generated content — data quality signal for web
post_en:
Wikipedia just banned AI-generated content. The world's largest encyclopedia now requires human authorship.

This isn't a reaction to bad AI writing. It's a data quality decision.

The problem Wikipedia identified:
→ AI-generated articles often contain confident-sounding fabrications
→ Citations get invented or misattributed
→ Subtle factual errors propagate through the knowledge graph
→ AI content trained on Wikipedia creates a feedback loop of degrading quality

Here's why the data industry should pay attention:

Wikipedia is the foundation dataset for almost every major AI model. When Wikipedia's quality degrades, AI outputs degrade across the board.

By banning AI content, Wikipedia is protecting not just its own integrity but the entire AI training data ecosystem.

The bigger signal: we're entering the "authenticity premium" era.

Human-verified, human-created content is becoming scarce — and therefore more valuable. Every dataset, every training corpus, every competitive intelligence report will need to answer: was this written by a human?

Data infrastructure that can verify content authenticity at collection time just became a critical capability.

#DataQuality #AIContent #WebData

Проблема:

→ Цитаты изобретаются или неправильно атрибутируются
→ Тонкие фактические ошибки распространяются по графу знаний
→ AI-контент, обученный на Wikipedia, создаёт петлю обратной связи деградации

Wikipedia — базовый датасет почти каждой крупной AI-модели. Когда качество Wikipedia падает, выходы AI деградируют повсеместно.

Мы входим в эру «премиума аутентичности». Верифицированный человеческий контент становится дефицитным — и более ценным.

Data-инфраструктура, способная верифицировать аутентичность контента при сборе, стала критической.

title: GitHub: We going to train on your data after all
summary: GitHub: We going to train on your data after all    theregister.com
editorial_override: GitHub will train on your data — massive training data ethics shift
post_en:
GitHub just announced it will use your Copilot interaction data to train AI models. By default. Unless you opt out.

Starting April 24, every code suggestion you accept, every prompt you type, every file you open with Copilot active becomes training data.

The details that matter:
→ This is OPT-OUT, not opt-in — you're included unless you actively change settings
→ It applies to all Copilot users on individual and business plans
→ The data includes your prompts, accepted suggestions, and surrounding code context
→ Enterprise plans are currently excluded

For the broader data industry, this is a template being replicated everywhere:

1. Build a product people love
2. Collect usage data as a byproduct
3. Change the terms to use that data for AI training
4. Make opting out possible but inconvenient

This is the new default across tech: your usage IS the training data.

Whether you're building code, writing documents, or browsing the web — the tools you use are harvesting your patterns to train the next model.

Data consent isn't a checkbox anymore. It's an ongoing negotiation.

#DataPrivacy #AITraining #GitHub

title: Web Bot Auth: What it is, how it works & how to test your bots
summary: Web Bot Auth lets bots cryptographically prove their identity. Learn how it works and use our free testing page to validate your implementation.
editorial_override: Web Bot Auth: what it is, how it works — bot detection infrastructure
post_en:
Web Bot Auth is here — and it could replace CAPTCHAs entirely.

A new authentication standard lets bots prove their identity and intent BEFORE accessing a website. Think of it as OAuth for machines.

How it works:
→ Bots register with a trusted authority and receive credentials
→ Each request includes a signed token declaring: who the bot is, what it wants, and who sent it
→ Websites verify the token and apply access policies in milliseconds
→ No CAPTCHAs, no fingerprinting, no cat-and-mouse games

Why this changes everything for data infrastructure:

Current bot detection is adversarial: websites try to catch bots, bots try to evade detection. It's expensive for both sides and creates an arms race nobody wins.

Web Bot Auth is cooperative: legitimate bots identify themselves, get appropriate access, and everyone benefits.

For proxy providers, this is a strategic inflection point:
→ Anonymous proxy traffic becomes increasingly blocked
→ Authenticated bot traffic gets premium access
→ The value shifts from "hiding identity" to "proving identity"

The proxy industry's next chapter isn't about better disguises. It's about better credentials.

#BotAuth #WebInfrastructure #DataAccess
post_ru:

Боты доказывают идентичность и намерение ДО доступа к сайту. OAuth для машин.

Как работает:
→ Боты регистрируются и получают credentials
→ Каждый запрос включает подписанный токен: кто бот, что хочет, кто отправил
→ Сайты верифицируют токен и применяют политики за миллисекунды
→ Никаких CAPTCHA, fingerprinting, кошки-мышки

Текущая бот-детекция — adversarial: сайты ловят ботов, боты уклоняются. Дорого для обеих сторон.

Web Bot Auth — cooperative: легитимные боты идентифицируются, получают доступ.

Для прокси-провайдеров — стратегический перелом:
→ Анонимный трафик всё больше блокируется
→ Аутентифицированный получает премиум-доступ
→ Ценность смещается от «скрыть идентичность» к «доказать идентичность»

#BotAuth #WebInfrastructure #DataAccess

"How are you handling web scraping at scale without getting blocked?"

This question just hit the front page — and the answers reveal how fast the landscape is shifting.

The consensus from hundreds of practitioners:

What stopped working in 2026:
→ Simple proxy rotation with datacenter IPs
→ Static user-agent spoofing
→ Fixed delay patterns between requests
→ Headless Chrome without proper fingerprint management

What actually works now:
→ Residential proxies with intelligent geo-targeting
→ Browser fingerprint randomization that matches real device distributions
→ AI-powered request timing that mimics human browsing patterns
→ Session management that maintains state across requests
→ Fallback chains: if one approach fails, automatically switch strategies

The recurring theme: brute force is dead. Intelligence is everything.

The teams succeeding at scale aren't spending more on infrastructure. They're spending more on SMART infrastructure — adaptive systems that respond to detection signals in real-time.

One practitioner summed it up perfectly: "The best scraper is one the target site never notices."

The data collection industry is no longer about volume. It's about precision.

#WebScraping #DataCollection #ProxyInfrastructure

title: Supreme Court Agrees With EFF: ISPs Don't Have To Be Copyright Enforcers
summary: If your ISP can be liable for huge amounts of money for not terminating your access to the internet because of accusations that you—or someone in your household or college network—has committed copyright infringement, that is dangerous. We live in a world where high speed internet access is a necessity for participation in everyday life. That’s why liability for ISPs for their customers’ actions should not be expanded. Last fall, EFF filed an amicus brief urging the U.S. Supreme Court to reject an expansive theory of secondary copyright liability that threatened to impose massive damages on internet service providers and other technology companies simply for offering widely used services. Yesterday, the Court agreed. In Cox v. Sony , the Court reversed a Fourth Circuit decision that had upheld a billion-dollar verdict against internet provider Cox Communications. Writing for the majority, Justice Thomas explained that contributory liability is limited to two situations: when a defendant actively induces infringement, or when it provides a product or service that it knows is tailored for infringement. This framework closely tracks the approach EFF urged in our amicus brief. As we explained, courts should look to patent law for guidance in defining the boundaries of secondary copyright liability. summary: Hi HN, I’ve been experimenting with ways to protect digital assets from automated AI web scrapers. I built Sigil, a local-first desktop application that embeds cryptographically signed ownership IDs into the LSB (Least Significant Bit) layer of images. The desktop vault itself (Svelte/Tauri/SQLite) is closed-source to protect the HMAC-SHA256 signing architecture, but I have open-sourced the Rust extraction standard today. The idea is to create an open protocol where AI data procurement teams can run the extractor against their scraped datasets. If it detects a payload, they know the asset is cryptographically locked and requires a license. The extractor logic relies entirely on image and hex crates for memory-safe pixel parsing. I'd love any feedback on the extraction architecture or the LSB approach. title: Show HN: Deepslate – a Minecraft server proxy written in Rust
summary: Finally sharing something that I've been casually working on for a month or so, and properly for the last week. Deepslate is a new solution for Minecraft server proxies (e.g. BungeeCord, Waterfall), written in Rust, with a focus on performance and a compile-time plugin system. Unlike most existing proxies, Deepslate takes a different approach where plugins are compiled into the binary, rather than loaded at runtime. This gives network operators full type safety at compile time, and minimal dispatch overhead. I've written an "Introducing Deepslate" blog post ( https://deepslatemc.com/intro/ ) which also covers some common questions, like what purpose a proxy has in Minecraft server networking, and some goals/non-goals of the project.
